exact_claim: The specified actual double tilts are bounded and satisfy Phi U_eta subset U_theta for independent endpoints on some open square for every 0<u<13/46, and on the radius-1/4000 square at uG.
hypotheses: X is a smooth complex quintic with hyperplane polarization, normalized characters and the ordered spherical-twist-after-tensor functor.
Xu arxiv:2511.21288v2 Theorem 1.3, only for actual positive-rank torsion-free slope-semistable sheaves with slope in [-1,1].
The explicitly inherited coherent-sheaf, noetherianity, slope HN, positivity, reflexive-hull, truncation and Serre-duality background.
The high/low quotient/subobject definitions and strict margins in report sections 3-5.
source_version: Old C55_AISLE v1, report sections 2-5; Gepner aisles.tex at reference revision 4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae
attribution: Reconstruction of the supplied manuscript's torsion-pair/comparison/twist mechanism, with proposed numerical strengthening using Xu directly; priority not checked.
decisive_argument: The actual B_- exact sequence with kernel S in the ordinary slope strip gives C>0,s*r(S)<=C,d(S)<=0 and error>=-3*delta*C, contradicting the nonpositive quotient/subobject cuts. The twist triangle and tensor shear then give the claimed independent comparison.
supported_scope: Bounded actual double tilts, heart positivity and exclusion of nonzero zero-class objects under the explicit background.
Comparison radius 1/4000 at uG and a positive radius for every 0<u<13/46.
13/46 is optimal for the two specified sufficient inequalities only.
limitations: The sheaf inequality and standard geometric package remain external assumptions.
The object-level torsion-pair, image and twist arguments are prose, not Lean theorems.
No necessity result for u<13/46 and no Gepner-eigencharge assertion for arbitrary u are supported.
